title: A quarter where three things slip at once
description: Over the same few weeks, about six weeks before the start date, three things change. A third of the paying learners stop opening lessons but keep signing in. Learners keep putting their next course in the cart, yet far fewer complete the checkout. And the three-person team answers learner questions more and more slowly, until half of the learners stop coming back to the Help page. The application stays fast and healthy throughout.

cases.title: Learners stop continuing their course
cases.what_changes: About a third of the paying learners stop opening lessons, but they keep signing in and looking at their progress.
cases.ai_agent: A lesson reminder: tells each inactive learner where they left off and links the next lesson.

cases.title: Courses left in the cart
cases.what_changes: Learners keep putting their next course in the cart, yet far fewer complete the checkout. About 145 learners end with courses waiting in their cart.
cases.ai_agent: A cart reminder: reminds each learner of the course waiting in their cart and links back to it.

cases.title: The team stops answering questions in time
cases.what_changes: Questions pile up on a few repetitive topics (certificates, invoices, accounts) and replies slow from hours to weeks, so learners stop coming back to Help.
cases.who: Staff and learners · for example Sofia Lindqvist (staff) and Lena Hoffmann
cases.ai_agent: Draft replies for the staff: prepares an answer to each repetitive open question for the team to check and send.

expected_finding: Three separate findings, each about fewer returning users on part of a different capability, each saying the application was healthy over the period. About 40% fewer learners open lessons in 'Course delivery and learner progress' (an AI agent could bring inactive learners back with a lesson reminder). About half as many learners complete the enrolment step of the checkout in the catalog and purchase capability, while nearly as many as before put courses in their cart (an AI agent could remind the roughly 145 learners whose courses wait in their cart). And about half as many learners come back to the Help page, in the capability that holds the learner notifications and Help (an AI agent could draft answers to the repetitive open questions for the staff to check and send).

verified_against.file: packages/modules/new-evolution-opportunity/drift/detectors.js (detectActorInactivity, actorDropVerdict) and constants.js (ACTOR_INACTIVITY_DROP_PCT = 33, MIN_INACTIVITY_ACTORS = 200, MIN_ACTOR_WINDOW_DAYS = 7, MAX_ACTOR_WINDOW_LENGTH_RATIO = 1.5, MIN_TREND_DAYS = 14)
verified_against.threshold: Learning (services/learning, the capability that holds the lesson routes): distinct client IPs on GET /api/lessons/{lessonId} and GET /api/courses/{courseId}/lessons fall 334 -> 193 (-42.2%) and on POST /api/lessons/{lessonId}/progress 334 -> 181..184 (-44.9..-45.8%), for start dates on all seven weekdays (days -59..-30 against -29..0). The capability-level max (GET /api/me/progress, read at every sign-in, about 410 -> 394) moves 3.7..4.4%, so the route-level fallback reports the lesson routes. Both windows are 30 days and every day is observed.

verified_against.file: packages/modules/new-evolution-opportunity/drift/detectors.js (detectActorInactivity: the route-level fallback names the qualifying route with the most earlier users)
verified_against.threshold: Catalog (services/catalog: cart and enrolment): distinct client IPs on POST /api/courses/{courseId}/enrol fall from 298..311 to 145..160 (-46.3..-52.9% on all seven start weekdays). The only other catalog route that moves is POST /api/me/cart/items (about 318 -> 290, -2.9..-15.3%), under the 33% bar, so the enrol route is the one named; GET /api/me/cart, GET /api/courses and GET /api/courses/{courseId} move under 5% (capability-level max -3.7..-4.4%). Learners who stopped opening lessons keep saving courses in the cart, which is why cart adds stay flat while lessons fall. data/seed/carts.json holds 140..155 learners with courses waiting in their cart.

Notifications (services/notifications, which also declares the learner Help routes): distinct client IPs on /api/me/support-requests (GET to read their questions and answers, POST to ask) fall from 290..307 to 148..155 (-46.6..-50.3% on all seven start weekdays). GET /api/me/notifications/unread-count (every sign-in, the capability-level max) moves 3.7..4.4%, GET /api/me/notifications 8.2..11.3% and POST /api/me/notifications/{notificationId}/read 7.4..12.3%, so the Help route is the one named. The staff side (GET /api/admin/support-requests and the reply route, declared in services/admin) comes from one office address, far under MIN_INACTIVITY_ACTORS, so it raises nothing on its own; staff open the queue about half as often and send about a third as many replies. data/seed/support_requests.json ends with 22..38 open questions, 94-100% of them about certificates, billing or the account, and the earlier answers carry real staff ids.

server errors stay at or below 0.05% per capability per window (under 0.4% on the worst route-day), far under INCIDENT_ERROR_RATE_PCT = 5, with no client errors on these routes and p95 about 105-131 ms on lesson routes and 55-63 ms elsewhere, unchanged at the drops, so incident_or_outage is ruled out, not confirmed; every hour of the 60 days has logs, so data_quality has no gap to confirm; the three changes are spread over days -45..-30 across several releases. None of the three is withdrawn.

NBF-USAGE-ACTOR_INACTIVITY is an 'agentic_candidate' (inactivity_churn), so for each of the three the solution architect may propose an AI agent: a lesson reminder (progress.json: last_activity_at of the learners who stopped), a cart reminder (carts.json), and replies drafted for staff to approve (support_requests.json: the open questions, and the earlier answers to the same questions).

verified_against.file: backend/src/cadence.js (continueAfterTelemetryIngest: the earlier window is read once per application), packages/platform/telemetry/ingestion.js (route baselines exist only for routes with requests in the window read), packages/modules/new-evolution-opportunity/drift/usage.js (actorWindowsOf: the highest distinct-user count per window is kept), detectors.js (actorDropVerdict: a route needs two measured windows)
verified_against.threshold: The staged reveal (staged_reveal below). One 'Get usage telemetry' reads days -29..0 again; days -59..-30 are read only when the application is onboarded (GA_TELEMETRY_HISTORY_WINDOWS = 1, and a later read finds that history already read). So every stage carries the final traffic of days -60..-30, and withholds only the recent traffic of the routes whose drop is a later case. A withheld route then has one measured window (too_few_measured_windows, no finding) until its stage brings its recent window; the routes already revealed are byte for byte the same in every stage, so the agent's max-per-window merge keeps their numbers and the stage-1 finding keeps its fingerprint (one live finding per code and capability: duplicate_live). Checked with the agent's own observationsForGoal over baselines built from each stage, start dates on all seven weekdays: stage 1 raises only the lesson finding, stage 2 adds the enrol finding (earlier 298..311 -> recent 145..160), stage 3 adds the Help finding (290..307 -> 148..155); the cart write routes are withheld with enrolment so that no goal-trend observation about purchases appears before stage 2.

staged_reveal.why: The presenter onboards LearnLoop once and reveals the three cases one at a time. The Governance Agent reads the earlier 30 days only when the application is onboarded and keeps the highest distinct-user count it has read for a window, so a stage may only add recent traffic, and the earlier 30 days must be final from the first stage on.

stages.expected_new_finding: One finding: about 42% fewer people open lessons in 'Course delivery and learner progress' (the lesson routes, 334 -> 193). Nothing about the store or Help yet.

A second finding, the first one still there: about half as many people complete the enrolment step of the checkout in the catalog and purchase capability (POST /api/courses/{courseId}/enrol, 298..311 -> 145..160).

A third finding, the first two still there: about half as many people come back to the Help page in the capability that holds the learner notifications and Help (/api/me/support-requests, 290..307 -> 148..155).
